reason: This text fragment (Exodus 3) records God's call to Moses at the burning bush. The passage focuses on God's compassion for the oppressed Israelites in Egypt, his identification with the God of the patriarchs, and his commission to Moses to lead the people out of Egypt. The only reference to worship ('תַּֽעַבְדוּן אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים' - 'you will serve/worship God') appears as a promised outcome after liberation, not as a conditional threat. There is no statement or implication that Yahweh will kill the Hebrews for improper worship in this passage. The text contains no threats of death based on worship practices.
